evals.prompt: I did git reset --hard and lost my last two commits. Should I just re-clone?
evals.expected_output: Tells the user not to re-clone, finds the pre-reset sha in the reflog, and restores it onto a new branch before moving the real branch.
expectations: Says not to re-clone or run gc
Creates a rescue branch or backup first
Uses git reflog to find the lost sha
Restores onto a new branch and verifies before resetting the working branch

evals.prompt: I pushed a commit with a bug to main. How do I undo it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends git revert on the shared branch instead of reset and force-push, with the merge variant if relevant.
expectations: Advises against reset + force-push on a shared branch
Mentions --force-with-lease only as a coordinated last resort

evals.prompt: I dropped a stash by accident with git stash drop. Is it gone?
evals.expected_output: Explains dropped stashes are unreachable commits, finds them with git fsck, and applies the right one.
expectations: Uses git fsck --unreachable (or equivalent) to find stash commits
Shows how to apply the recovered stash
Warns against running gc before recovery

evals.prompt: I edited a file for an hour but never saved it to git, then ran git checkout on it. Can you recover it?
evals.expected_output: Explains git never recorded unstaged edits and points to editor local history instead, without promising recovery from git.
expectations: States git cannot recover never-staged changes
Suggests editor local history (VS Code Timeline, JetBrains Local History)
Does not invent a git command that claims to restore it
